title: Explicit rate limit semantics and idempotency surface for OpenAI-compatible adapter
author: Priya Sinha
description:
Motivation: Clients expect stable, documented semantics for rate limits and idempotency when talking to our OpenAI-compat adapter. Previous behavior left ambiguity around which headers/fields are authoritative (Retry-After vs X-RateLimit-Reset), how duplicated requests for streaming endpoints are handled, and how server errors map to OpenAI-style error objects. This change makes the adapter's behavior explicit, documents compatibility guarantees, and adds tests to prevent regressions.

Summary of changes: 1) Rate limit semantics: adapter now consistently prefers the standard Retry-After header (seconds) for upstream throttling and mirrors it into the OpenAI error body as error.retry_after_seconds (integer). We also surface X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset (when available) under the X-RW-Rate-* headers for internal telemetry, but these are not considered authoritative for client retry logic. 2) Error shape: All adapter errors returned to OpenAI-compatible clients follow a single canonical shape: {"error":{"message":string,"type":string,"code":string,"param":string|null,"retry_after_seconds":int|null}}. This replaces ad-hoc bodies and maps internal error categories to OpenAI-friendly codes (rate_limit -> rate_limit_exceeded, conflict -> duplicate_request, internal -> server_error, invalid -> invalid_request_error). 3) Idempotency behavior: adapter accepts Idempotency-Key (case-insensitive). When present we: - atomically record a request fingerprint + response pointer in the dedupe store (Redis) with TTL (configurable, default 24h). - If a duplicate arrives and the original completed successfully: return the same HTTP status + body as the original (including same error envelope). - If a duplicate arrives while the original is still in flight: return 409 with code duplicate_request_in_progress and include header X-RW-Idempotency-Status: in_progress. - If a duplicate is detected but the new request parameters differ: return 409 conflict with message 'idempotency key collision: differing payloads'. - For streaming endpoints, successful responses are persisted as a replayable stream reference; duplicates will stream the recorded bytes so clients receive the identical sequence of chunk events and closing sentinel. 4) Streaming and partial failures: if an original stream failed mid-flight, subsequent duplicates will receive a deterministic error (code incomplete_stream) and an indication whether the client can safely retry (field can_retry in the error body). 5) Downstream propagation: internal calls now receive X-RW-Idempotency header when Idempotency-Key is present; this allows downstream systems to participate in dedupe semantics. 6) Backwards compatibility: behavior is gated behind the OpenAI-Compat-Version header (>= 2026-02) or the adapter flag openai_compat_strict: true. Without that header/flag, legacy behavior is preserved.

Files changed (high level): openai_adapter/handler.py (idempotency and retry handling), openai_adapter/errors.py (canonical error shapes and mappers), openai_adapter/stream_replay.py (stream persistence + replay), docs/openai-compat.md (compatibility matrix + examples), tests/test_idempotency.py (unit), tests/e2e_stream_replay.py (integration), ci/fixtures/idempotency.json (examples).

Rollout plan: - Deploy to staging with strict flag enabled for a subset of routes. - Run e2e stream replay and idempotency tests against staging. - Gradually enable for customers who specify OpenAI-Compat-Version or opt-in via account flag. - Monitor metrics: idempotency_hits, idempotency_collisions, rate_limit_retry_after_distribution.

Testing: unit coverage added for error mapping and idempotency collision detection; integration test reproduces a duplicated streaming request and asserts identical chunk sequence and final event. Load test exercised Retry-After handling across Nginx + upstream to validate header precedence.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test for stream replay - [x] Docs updated with examples and migration notes - [x] Rollout plan included - [x] Telemetry counters added

Backward compatibility notes: clients not opting into the new compat version will not observe the stricter semantics. We intentionally limit change-surface to prevent breaking existing integrations.

References: Linear ENG-4812 (idempotency design), ENG-4820 (stream replay), SUP-3321 (support case prompting clarifications).

review_thread: Evan Park (requested changes): Can you include a short TTL rationale for the dedupe store? 24h seems generous for some customers. Also add a metric for dedupe ttl expiries.
Author (Priya Sinha): TTL made configurable with default 24h; added metric idempotency_ttl_expiries and documentation explaining tradeoffs. Suggested shorter TTLs for high-volume endpoints.
Miguel Alvarez (comment): For streaming replay, what guarantees do we provide around event ids and chunks? We should avoid leaking internal offsets.
Author (Priya Sinha): Stream replay now uses a stable event-id namespace derived from request fingerprint; we do not expose upstream offsets. Added tests to verify event-id determinism.
Zoe Chen (approved): Security + privacy note: ensure persisted stream blobs are encrypted at rest and honored by retention policy. Please add an ops runbook for manual revoke.
Author (Priya Sinha): Added encryption note and ops runbook link in docs.
release_notes: Added explicit OpenAI-compatible rate limit and idempotency semantics: standardized error envelope, idempotency-key handling for streaming and unary requests, and a gated rollout via OpenAI-Compat-Version. See docs/openai-compat.md for migration guidance.
